contracts.description: The stuck-session check: a total function from (sessions, state, now, config) to (alerts, state) — detection predicate, observation clock, threshold with a wire-format-pinned default, once-per-episode alerting, and state lifecycle.

exclusions: Payload acquisition: invoking claude agents --json, CLI errors, timeouts, malformed JSON — the binding feeds check a parsed array or does not call it.
Scheduling and process management: poll interval, systemd units, timer placement.
Alert delivery and formatting: Discord webhooks, message wording, retries — bindings render the alert set; the set is contract, the prose is not.
Remediation: killing, attaching to, or answering stuck sessions (claude kill <id> is the binding's business).

Re-alert reminders and recovery notification: a continuously-stuck session alerts once per episode and a session leaving the stuck state emits nothing at 0.1.0 — deferred, not refused; arrives as proposed criteria via promotion if wanted.
Interactive-session UX: prompts answered at a keyboard are normal operation.
Alert ordering beyond ASCII sessionIds: the CLI emits ASCII UUIDs, on which code-point and UTF-16 code-unit comparisons agree; orderings that differ only for non-ASCII ids are not contract surface.

Nonconforming state input: a conforming binding persists exactly the state check emitted, so check is never presented a state outside watchdog/state@0; behavior over such values is excluded, not defined.
goals: A stuck background session is invisible to exit-code alerting: the unit exits 0, OnFailure never fires, the session holds memory until someone notices. The watchdog makes wait-states observable.
The core is a pure check function over (sessions payload, state, clock): every transition is fixtured; polling, delivery, and remediation live outside it.
Conformance is derived from recorded evidence against this spec's fixtures, never asserted bare.
name: watchdog-core

body:
The watchdog core is one total function, check: (sessions, state, now, config?) -> (alerts, state).

Wire format watchdog/check-input@0: sessions is the parsed JSON array emitted by `claude agents --json` — records are opaque JSON objects; the fields this contract reads are sessionId (string; hygiene for elements that violate this is it-wd-input's), kind, status, waitingFor, and startedAt; all other fields pass through untouched. state is watchdog/state@0 (see it-wd-state). now is the current instant as epoch milliseconds UTC. config is optional: {thresholdSeconds?: non-negative integer}. The default thresholdSeconds=1800 is pinned in this wire format, not in any spec record, config file, or binding, and applies whenever config is absent, carries no thresholdSeconds, or carries a thresholdSeconds that is not a non-negative integer (null, negative, fractional, string — all treated as absent): config shares the totality stance of sessions; check never raises. Non-negative integer means the mathematical value, not the lexeme: a number equal to its floor and >= 0 qualifies however the source text spelled it. The null, negative, and string cases are fixtured; the fractional case is stated but not fixturable — this interchange's canonical form (felag CS6) cannot represent a non-integer numeral in a fixture payload, a residue filed against felag from this compilation. Result wire format watchdog/check-result@0: {alerts, state}.

Detection predicate: a payload record is WAITING iff kind=="background" AND status=="waiting". The waitingFor text is never matched — it is free prose ('permission prompt' today, anything tomorrow), and a background session waiting on anything is equally dead: nothing will ever answer it. Interactive sessions never alert and never enter state: a prompt at a keyboard is normal operation. The predicate keys off status, not state=="blocked": status is the CLI's explicit wait signal; blocked is a coarser lifecycle value whose other inhabitants are unknown. status is authoritative in both directions — a background record with state "blocked" but status anything-other-than-"waiting" is not WAITING, and a background record with status "waiting" is WAITING whatever its state value.

The clock starts at observation, not at startedAt: the payload carries no waiting-since timestamp (verified against the claude CLI, 2026-06-12), so the first poll that observes a session WAITING records firstSeenWaiting=now in its state entry. Evaluation within a poll is single-pass: a WAITING record's entry is its existing state entry when present, otherwise a new entry with firstSeenWaiting=now created by this poll, and the alert condition is evaluated against that entry — so with thresholdSeconds=0 a session alerts on the very poll that first observes it. A WAITING session alerts iff its entry carries no alertedAt AND now - firstSeenWaiting >= thresholdSeconds*1000 — instant arithmetic on epoch milliseconds, >= so the boundary alerts. A firstSeenWaiting in the future (clock skew) yields a negative age and cannot alert; check never rewrites firstSeenWaiting to compensate. An emitted alert is {"session": <the payload record verbatim>, "stuckSince": <the entry's firstSeenWaiting>} and sets alertedAt=now on the entry. alerts is sorted ascending by session.sessionId in Unicode code-point order (the CLI's session ids are ASCII UUIDs, on which every common string comparison agrees; ids are compared as opaque strings); check emits no other output.
interfaceSketch: check(input: {sessions: unknown[], state: WatchdogState, now: number, config?: {thresholdSeconds?: number}}): {alerts: Alert[], state: WatchdogState} — pure, total, no I/O.
title: The check function

gherkin:
Given a background session with status waiting whose state entry's firstSeenWaiting is at least thresholdSeconds*1000 before now and carries no alertedAt
When check runs
Then alerts contains exactly {session: the payload record verbatim, stuckSince: firstSeenWaiting} and the entry gains alertedAt=now

Given a background session with status waiting whose entry is younger than the threshold
When check runs
Then alerts is empty and the entry's firstSeenWaiting is retained unchanged

Given a positive thresholdSeconds and a background session with status waiting and no state entry, however old its startedAt
When check runs
Then alerts is empty and a new entry records firstSeenWaiting=now

Given background records whose state says blocked while status does not say waiting, background records with status waiting and a non-blocked state, and interactive records waiting on prompts
When check runs
Then only kind background with status waiting is tracked or alerted — status is authoritative; state and kind alone never qualify

Given a background session waiting on something other than a permission prompt, past the threshold
When check runs
Then it alerts exactly as a permission-prompt wait does

Given config absent, present without thresholdSeconds, or carrying a thresholdSeconds that is not a non-negative integer
When a waiting session's observed age reaches exactly 1800 seconds
Then it alerts at the boundary and does not alert one second short of it

Given two or more sessions alert in the same poll
When check runs
Then alerts is sorted ascending by session.sessionId in code-point order

body:
`claude agents --json` is an external surface this contract does not control; check is total over arbitrary JSON arrays. Two hygiene rules, restated mechanically:

A payload element that is not a JSON object — null, a number, a string, an array — and a payload record whose sessionId is absent or not a string are ignored entirely: they never alert, never enter state, and never raise an error; valid records in the same payload are processed normally.

If several records share a sessionId, the last in array order is the session's effective record: the WAITING predicate is evaluated against it, and an emitted alert carries it verbatim. Earlier duplicates contribute nothing — when the last record is not WAITING, the session is not tracked, whatever earlier duplicates say.
title: Payload hygiene

gherkin:
Given payload elements that are not JSON objects, and records whose sessionId is absent or not a string
When check runs
Then they are ignored entirely — no alert, no state entry, no error — and valid records in the same payload are processed normally

Given several payload records sharing a sessionId
When check runs
Then the last record in array order is the session's effective record — an emitted alert carries it verbatim, and when the last record is not waiting the session is not tracked, whatever earlier duplicates say

body:
Wire format watchdog/state@0: {"sessions": {<sessionId>: {"firstSeenWaiting": <epoch ms>, "alertedAt": <epoch ms, present iff an alert has been emitted this episode>}}}.

The result state contains exactly one entry per distinct sessionId whose effective record (it-wd-input) is WAITING (it-wd-check), and no others: entries for sessions that are absent from the payload, no longer waiting, or not background are removed. State can therefore never grow without bound.

An episode is an unbroken run of polls observing a session WAITING. Entry creation precedes alert evaluation within a poll (it-wd-check): an episode can be born and alert in the same poll when the threshold permits. Within an episode firstSeenWaiting is stable — a poll never rewrites it — and alertedAt, once set, is retained verbatim: at most one alert per episode. A session observed not WAITING ends its episode by removal; observed WAITING again later, that is a new episode — the clock restarts and one new alert may eventually fire.

The wire format is one poll. Multi-poll behavior composes by determinism: the corpus pins every single-poll transition (creation, continuation, alert, suppression, removal), and composition introduces no state beyond watchdog/state@0. Worked example, each step a pinned transition: poll 1 observes waiting (entry created); poll 2 alerts past threshold (alertedAt set); poll 3 still waiting (suppressed); poll 4 session gone (entry removed); poll 5 waiting again (fresh entry, new episode); poll 6 past threshold (one new alert). The state is the caller's to persist between polls; the binding owns the file's location and the empty initial value {"sessions":{}}.
title: Episode state

gherkin:
Given thresholdSeconds 0 and a waiting background session with no state entry
When check runs
Then the entry is created with firstSeenWaiting=now and one alert fires in the same poll with stuckSince=now

Given a waiting background session whose entry carries alertedAt
When check runs
Then alerts is empty and the entry is retained verbatim

Given a state entry for a background session the payload reports not waiting
When check runs
Then the entry is removed from the result state

Given a state entry whose sessionId appears nowhere in the payload
When check runs
Then the entry is removed from the result state
